newsitem.title: MEXICO: Tampico area named for Mexico natgas privatization.
newsitem.headline: Tampico area named for Mexico natgas privatization.

text.p: Mexico's Energy Regulatory Commission on Thursday announced that the region surrounding the city of Tampico in Tamaulipas state would be opened to private natural gas distribution.
The commission said in the Official Gazette that use of natural gas will be encouraged in port cities Tampico and Altamira and the region along the Panuco river.
Mexico is setting up zones to auction off to private companies concessions to distribute natural gas.
The Tamaulipas state region on the border of Veracruz state does not have a comprehensive natural gas distribution system, the gazette said.

All natural gas is supplied by state oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex). Gas is currently distributed through 12- to 16-inch ducts connected to a main pipeline that runs through the region, the gazette said.
The commission did not say when it would invite companies to bid for the distribution concession but said it already had heard from groups interested in the region.
"It is located in an area with companies ... whose principal energy consumption is in natural gas and electricity," the commission said.
The designated region's population was 515,606 in 1990 with the population expected to rise to 1.24 million by 2000, according to a census.
A decision on another region to be auctioned, in Chihuahua state, is expected by March 20.
